- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.5) and underperform in the short term after spikes.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially <0.3) and overreact to recent volatility.
- Model tends to lag in upward trends — forecast peaks too late, especially after sentiment shifts to bullish.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes — model overreacts to recent highs, leading to overprediction in next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: model often forecasts prices to stay high after a spike, ignoring recent downward momentum.
- Sentiment-driven bias: if sentiment is high, model tends to overforecast; if sentiment is low, underforecast — especially in the first 5–7 days of forecast horizon.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to underestimating late-period volatility, especially when sentiment is bullish and price is trending upward.
